steps.title: Start with the reference tetrahedron
steps.explanation: Unit stretches and zero shear prescribe the identity map. Compare the determinant with volume measured independently from the closed boundary triangles.
steps.observe: Both volume ratios are 1; Green strain is zero up to floating-point roundoff. The coincident surfaces are expected.

steps.title: Lengthen one direction
steps.explanation: Only the X direction is stretched. The transverse stretches stay 1, so det F = 1.2 × 1 × 1 = 1.2.
steps.observe: Both volume ratios become 1.2. Green strain norm is 0.22; these are imposed geometric changes, not a force response.

steps.title: Change shape while keeping volume
steps.explanation: Restore axial stretch to 1 and impose shear 0.25. The triangular deformation matrix still has unit determinant, but its reference Y-directed edge becomes longer.
steps.observe: J stays 1 while Green strain norm is about 0.179518 and Y-line stretch is about 1.03078. Constant volume does not mean zero strain.

steps.title: Rotate without adding strain
steps.explanation: Rotate the same sheared geometry by 90 degrees. Rigid rotation changes world-space positions but preserves edge lengths and F-transpose F.
steps.observe: The geometry rotates; J, Green strain norm and Y-line stretch match the previous step. No material law or equilibrium has been introduced.

audit.finding: Hidden transverse stretches and rotation made the previous unit-axial control state non-reference; only volume was reported.
audit.change: Use explicit unit transverse stretches, a rotation control, Green strain and line-stretch diagnostics in an identity/stretch/shear/rotation sequence.
audit.remaining: Prescribed affine kinematics only. No constitutive energy, equilibrium, curved-element validity or physiological calibration.
